question: In coup-contre-coup brain injury, the coup injury (at the site of impact) is always more severe than the contre-coup injury (at the side opposite the impact).

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: Incorrect. Contra to intuition, the contre-coup lesion is typically more severe in moving-head injuries against a fixed surface. This is because brain inertia causes maximum shear strain at the pole opposite the impact point. Coup injury severity predominates only when a moving object strikes a stationary head.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. The contre-coup injury is classically more severe than the coup injury when the moving head strikes a stationary surface. The brain lags behind skull deceleration, shearing the brain against the opposite inner surface. Coup lesions may be minimal while contre-coup contusions are the dominant finding.
